item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 231149
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Wed Sep 23 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located a couple of hundred miles offshore of southern
Mexico, on recently upgraded Hurricane Odalys, located well
west-southwest of the southern tip of Baja California, and on
recently re-formed Tropical Depression Fifteen-E, located a few
hundred miles south-southeast of the Big Island of Hawaii.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec:
An area of low pressure is expected to form in a couple of days to
the south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Afterwards, environmental
conditions should be favorable for gradual development, and a
tropical depression is likely to form late this week or this weekend
as the system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward,
parallel to the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

&&

Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Fifteen-E are issued under
WMO header WTPA32 PHFO and under AWIPS header TCPCP2.
Forecast/Advisoires on Tropical Depression Fifteen-E are issued
under WMO header WTPA22 PHFO and under AWIPS header TCMCP2.

$$
Forecaster Blake

--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Odalys was located
near latitude 16.0 North, longitude 127.9 West. Odalys is moving
toward the east-northeast near 8 mph (13 km/h).  An eastward to
east-northeastward motion at a slightly slower speed is expected
for the next couple of days, followed by a gradual turn toward
the northeast then north later this week.

Maximum sustained winds are near 75 mph (120 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Additional strengthening is expected during the
next day or two, followed by a weakening trend late this week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 10 miles (20 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).

item.title: Hurricane Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Wed Sep 23 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 230841
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Odalys Discussion Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 AM PDT Wed Sep 23 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that Odalys has recovered from the 
earlier dry air intrusion. Deep convection has developed over the 
low-level center, with a convective shield that has cold cloud tops 
near -80 C. In addition, a recent WSF-M microwave pass revealed a 
nearly closed low-level convective ring and a developing eye 
feature. A subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB has 
increased to T4.0/65 kt, and objective intensity estimates from 
UW-CIMSS range between 55 and 68 kt. Based on these estimates and 
the improved structural organization in the microwave data, the 
initial intensity is set at 65 kt, making Odalys a hurricane.
 
The initial motion is estimated to be east-northeastward, or 065/8 
kt. This general motion is expected to continue in the short term as 
Odalys is steered by the flow between a mid- to upper-level trough 
moving into the eastern Pacific and a strong ridge located over 
central Mexico. A turn toward the northeast and then north is 
forecast in a couple of days. Beyond day 3, the steering pattern 
becomes increasingly complex, and potential interaction with 
Hurricane Polo will likely complicate the future track of Odalys. 
The updated NHC track forecast is near the previous advisory, and 
lies near the previous the HCCA and GDMI track aids.
 
Vertical wind shear is forecast to begin relaxing as Odalys 
traverses warm sea surface temperatures, which should allow for 
steady strengthening over the next 24 to 36 hours. By 48 to 72 
hours, wind shear is forecast to increase once again, SSTs will 
cool, and Odalys may begin to experience upper-level outflow from 
Hurricane Polo. At the same time, the cyclone will move into a drier 
mid-level environment, which should induce a weakening trend. The 
official NHC intensity forecast shows a slightly higher peak 
intensity, and is closest to the HCCA and GDMI intensity aids. 
Toward the end of the forecast period, model-simulated infrared 
satellite imagery indicates that Odalys will succumb to a drier 
environment. As the system becomes devoid of organized deep 
convection, it is expected to degenerate into a post-tropical 
cyclone, which is now shown in the latest NHC forecast at day 5.

item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Wed Sep 23 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 231443
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Advisory Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
900 AM CST Wed Sep 23 2026
 
...POLO NOW MOVING SLOWLY NORTHWESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM CST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.4N 101.8W
ABOUT 160 MI...255 KM S OF ZIHUATANEJO MEXICO
ABOUT 300 MI...480 KM SE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...150 MPH...240 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...927 MB...27.38 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Tecpan de Galeana to Punta San Telmo
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* West of Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within 12
hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere along the southwestern Mexico coast should
continue to monitor the progress of this system as additional
watches and warnings could be necessary later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM CST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Polo was located
near latitude 15.4 North, longitude 101.8 West. Polo is now moving
toward the northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this motion is 
expected to continue through Thursday. A general west-northwestward 
motion is forecast on Friday and over the weekend. On the forecast 
track, the core of Polo is expected to be near the coast of 
southwestern Mexico during the next day or two, although it is 
forecast to remain offshore.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 150 mph (240 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Polo is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale.  Fluctuations in intensity are expected, but
Polo is expected to remain a very powerful major hurricane during
the next few days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles
(165 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 927 mb (27.38 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected within the warning
area along the coast of Mexico later today. Tropical storm
conditions are possible within the watch area along the coast of
Mexico on Thursday.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 6
inches, with isolated maximum totals up to 8 inches across coastal
portions of the Mexican state of Guerrero through Thursday. This
rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides,
especially in areas of steep terrain. Rainfall of 2 to 4 inches is
possible in coastal portions of the Mexican states of Michoacan,
Colima, and Jalisco through Thursday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Polo are expected to affect portions of
the coast of southwestern Mexico during the next few days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf, rip current
conditions, and coastal flooding. Please consult products from
your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1200 PM CST.
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Wed Sep 23 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 231444
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
900 AM CST Wed Sep 23 2026

Satellite imagery this morning indicates that Polo is continuing to 
undergo an eyewall replacement cycle, with infrared imagery showing 
multiple rings of cold tops near and around the center. Overall, 
the hurricane is not as intense as it was 24 h ago, as the eye has 
become less distinct and the eyewall cloud tops have warmed. The 
various satellite intensity estimates have trended downward, and 
based on this trend the initial intensity is lowered to a possibly 
generous 130 kt.  Outer rainbands in the northeastern semicircle 
have reached the coast of Mexico.

Polo is starting its forecast turn toward the northwest with the 
initial motion now 325/4 kt.  Water vapor imagery suggests a 
mid-level ridge is building over Texas and Mexico, and the 
dynamical models forecast this ridge to build westward to the north 
of Polo for the next 2-3 days. This evolution should result in Polo 
moving northwestward and then west-northwestward with some increase 
in forward speed. The forecast becomes more uncertain after 60-72 
h. The dynamical models forecast the ridge to the north to weaken
around that time as a mid-latitude trough moves into the western 
United States. There is also the possibility of interaction with 
Hurricane Odalys to the west. The guidance becomes divergent by 
120 h, with the GFS/HCCA/Google DeepMind/Florida State 
Superensemble showing a northward motion close to Baja California, 
while the regional hurricane models/UKMET/Canadian show a 
northwestward motion farther away from Baja.  The track forecast 
goes with the northward motion scenario, but there is a significant 
amount of uncertainty in this portion of the forecast.

The trends of the intensity forecast guidance suggest that Polo 
could weaken a little during the next day or so, followed by 
re-intensification during the ensuing 24 h. The first two days of 
the intensity forecast follow these trends, and there could be 
fluctuations in intensity due to eyewall replacement cycles 
superimposed on top of this overall trend. After 48 h, the 
environment gradually becomes less favorable due to slightly 
stronger shear and the possibility of some dry air entrainment. The 
guidance forecast slow weakening during this time, and the new 
intensity forecast follows suit. The new forecast is near the upper 
edge of the guidance for the first 60 h and then lies closer to the 
middle of the guidance envelope.

While the center of Polo is forecast to remain offshore, outer 
rainbands should spread across southwestern Mexico during the next 
day or so, producing areas of heavy rain and tropical-storm-force 
winds.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will impact coastal portions 
of southwest Mexico through Thursday. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.
 
2. A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for portions of
southwestern Mexico, and a Tropical Storm Watch is in effect
westward to Playa Perula. Interests in these areas should closely
monitor updates to the forecast.
